newsitem.title: USA: Gephardt names union official to gambling panel.
newsitem.headline: Gephardt names union official to gambling panel.

text.p: House Democratic leader Richard Gephardt named Wednesday his appointee to a gambling study commission -- a union official who has represented workers whose livelihoods depend on the gambling industry.
Gephardt named John Wilhelm, Secretary-Treasurer of the Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees International Union, saying it was important for workers to have a voice on the national commission.
"John brings broad experience representing the thousands and thousands of employees whose jobs and livelihoods depend on the future of the industry," Gephardt said in a statement.

"The National Gambling Impact Study Commission has an important charge: to examine the impact of gambling and gaming on the economy and our people. Every affected group -- from the operators to the employees to the communities -- deserves to have their voice heard," Gephardt said.
Congress last July passed a bill to establish a national commission to study the impact of gambling on U.S. society.

The commission will have nine members, three appointed by the president and three each by House and Senate leaders. Gephardt's announcement wrapped up the Capitol Hill appointments; President Clinton has yet to make his.
Wilhelm is considered pro-casino by the National Coalition against Legalized Gambling, a grassroots organization dedicated to stopping the spread of legalized gambling.
